findings.description: TAIL-TRUNCATE IS A FAKE-ONLY GUARANTEE — the spec's "a human-inserted row ... is overwritten by design" is NOT honored on the real path. Spec: the tab is "regenerated" and inserted rows are overwritten. Code: `ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view` (crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs:205-238) issues exactly ONE `self.api.update_range("'<tab>'!A2:Z", &grid)` and never calls `clear_range`. The real primitive (crates/runtime/src/sheets.rs:510) is a plain `spreadsheets.values.update` PUT with `valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED`, which writes only the N rows supplied and leaves every residual row below untouched. The truncation exists ONLY in the two fakes: `FakeSheetsApi::update_range` does `grid.truncate(start)` then pushes (crates/runtime/src/testkit.rs:198-203), and `InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view` does `existing.rows = tab.rows.clone()` (crates/sheets-view/src/testkit.rs:178). `clear_range` is documented at crates/runtime/src/sheets.rs:148-150 as the "view-tab tail-truncate" primitive and is called by ZERO production code (only the testkit implements it). Both directions land on this: A-side implementations all shrink the grid explicitly (A1 `UpdateSheetProperties{row_count}`, A2 `ResizeGrid`, A3 whole-sheet `UpdateCells{fields:"*"}`), and all three B-side reconstructions confidently assert "truncating the residual tail to the exact new row count (2 rows → 1 row leaves exactly 1)" — a guarantee they read off the fakes and off doc-comments, not off shippable behavior. Failure: a portfolio that shrinks from 8 positions to 5, or a human-inserted row at row 9, leaves rows 7-9 of the prior render alive on the real Sheets tab under the frozen header, indistinguishable from live data.

FILTER-VIEW RE-ASSERTION IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. Spec's central affirmative clause: "republish actively re-asserts saved Sheets Filter Views so they persist across the rewrite." Code: `grep -rniE "filter.?view"` over the whole workspace returns zero hits. The `SheetsViewClient` trait (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:426-465) exposes exactly four methods — `batch_update_view`, `set_tab_order`, `read_price_pass`, `write_stale_banner` — with no seam through which a filter view could be read, created, or re-asserted; `SheetsApi` (crates/runtime/src/sheets.rs) offers only read_range/update_range/clear_range/ensure_sheet/append_rows_raw, i.e. the values grid only. All three A-runs built the mechanism unprompted (A1 delete-all + `AddFilterView`; A2 and A3 `UpdateFilterView`-by-title else `AddFilterView`), because the spec names it explicitly. Note the subtlety: because the code's republish is values-only, saved FilterViews probably survive *incidentally* today — but the spec commits to an ACTIVE re-assert precisely because the rewrite is supposed to be able to clobber them, and every doc-comment in the code claims the write is an "atomic batchUpdate" (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:427, adapters.rs:209). The day that claim becomes true structurally, the promised persistence breaks silently with no test guarding it.

"READ-ONLY" IS UNENFORCED — no protection mechanism of any kind. Spec: "The view tabs shall be read-only." Code: no `ProtectedRange`, no `AddProtectedRange`, no `warningOnly`, no editor/ACL handling anywhere in the workspace; the only occurrence of the phrase in sheets-view is the prose doc-comment at crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:3 ("Regenerates clean, read-only, filterable view tabs"). All three A-runs independently implemented a full-sheet `ProtectedRange` with `warning_only=false` (A1 assumption 3, A2 assumption 4, A3 assumption 1), and A1/A3 additionally sequence delete-protection-before-write / re-add-after, which the real code has no analogue for. As shipped, "read-only" means only "whatever you type inside A2:Z may be overwritten on the next sync" — and per finding 1 it often will not even be that.

FROZEN-HEADER CARVE-OUT: the code's real regeneration boundary is row 2 down, which the spec's flat "regenerated" never states or exempts. `DATA_START_ROW: u32 = 2` (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:148); every write targets `'<tab>'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` (adapters.rs:199-201). Row 1 is written EXACTLY ONCE, on the missing-tab bootstrap branch (`ensure_sheet` → `update_range("'<tab>'!A1", [header])` → retry data write, adapters.rs:225-235), and never again. `InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view` enforces byte-identical headers across republishes with a bare `assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header, "the frozen header must never be rewritten on republish")` — deliberately unconditional in all builds, not `debug_assert` (crates/sheets-view/src/testkit.rs:172-179), and pinned by `republish_regenerates_data_and_never_rewrites_frozen_header` (tests/tabs.rs:181-218). All three B-runs led with this. The spec grants no header exemption and states no header-stability contract, so a schema change to any of POSITIONS_HEADER / OPEN_LOTS_HEADER / REALIZED_HEADER / TAX_HEADER is a panic against an existing workbook with nothing in the EARS warning of it.

PER-TAB FAILURE / STALENESS PROTOCOL, wholly unstated by the spec — and it plants a cell that survives the very rewrite the spec calls total. `Publisher::republish` (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:954-999): on `batch_update_view` Err it sets `all_ok=false`, inserts the tab name into the stale set, writes a best-effort banner formatted exactly `"STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}"`, CONTINUES with the remaining tabs, and returns `RepublishOutcome{published:false, stale_tabs}`; on Ok it CLEARS the tab's stale flag. The banner write is discarded with `let _ = ...` (line 985) so its failure is swallowed. The adapter anchors the banner at `'{tab}'!AA1` (adapters.rs:286) — outside the rewritten `A2:Z` window, so a STALE banner from a past failure persists on the tab through every subsequent successful republish with nothing to clear it. All three B-runs reproduced the banner text, the AA1 anchor, the continue-then-report shape, and the swallow; B3 explicitly noted the banner "survives republishes."

ADVISORY WRITE-LOCK PRECONDITION, absent from the spec. `Publisher::republish` takes `lock: &L` and does `let _guard = match lock.acquire() { Ok(g) => g, Err(_) => return RepublishOutcome{published:false, stale_tabs: self.stale_tabs()} }` BEFORE any workbook mutation (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:964-972), so a held/erroring lock yields a fully non-destructive refusal: nothing written, stale set unchanged, retry next sync. Pinned by tests/republish.rs `republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating` and `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing`. All three B-runs stated it as a requirement; SHEET-TAB-003 says nothing about concurrency, single-writer discipline, or refusal semantics.

WORKBOOK TAB-ORDER REASSERT is bundled into republish and gates its success flag — spec never mentions ordering. `workbook_tab_order()` (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs:75-92) pins an exact 10-entry sequence: Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax, History, Tax Rules, Residency, Platforms & Aliases, Ledger Events, Tax Events. `republish` calls `set_tab_order(&order)` after the tab loop and downgrades `published` to false on failure WITHOUT flagging any tab stale (lines 991-994) — a distinct outcome all three B-runs called out (B2 VIEW-PUB-6, B3 X3). Pinned by `republish_idempotently_reasserts_tab_order` (tests/tabs.rs:160-178). Note the real adapter's `set_tab_order` is a hardcoded `Ok(())` no-op (adapters.rs:240-246), so the ordering intent the tests assert is never exercised against Sheets at all.

BASIC FILTER AND MANUAL SORT ARE NEVER CLEARED. Spec: "a basic filter, a manual sort ... on a view tab is overwritten by design." Code: no `ClearBasicFilter` or equivalent exists; the publish path touches only the values grid via `values.update`. A Sheets basic filter and its sort state are sheet-level metadata objects that a values write does not disturb — so a human-applied basic filter and sort persist indefinitely across every republish, and the rows silently change identity underneath the still-active sort, which is worse than the spec's promised overwrite. All three A-runs emitted an unconditional `Request::ClearBasicFilter` as step one (A1, A2, A3), A2 explicitly treating a no-basic-filter error as a no-op rather than fatal.

PUBLISHED-SURFACE SHAPE AND THE NO-AMONG-DATA-ROWS RULE, entirely code-side. `VIEW_TABS: [&str;4]` fixes the four names (lib.rs:70); the Tax surface additionally emits a FIFTH band, `TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary"` under `TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` (7 columns), returned as a separate `ViewTab` inside `TaxView` and explicitly NOT a fifth `VIEW_TABS` entry (lib.rs:47-52, 707-750). tests/tabs.rs:59-85 and :89-124 pin that the accrual band contains no blank row, no `"RESERVE SUMMARY"` label row, and no embedded `TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` masquerading as data, and that every row is exactly header-width. All three B-runs reconstructed this band separation as a requirement. The spec says only "view tabs" — it names no tabs, no count, no band split, and no one-row-per-entity/native-filterability rule, even though that rule is the actual mechanism by which the tabs stay filterable (the property the spec attributes to Filter Views instead). Separately, `Publisher::republish` accepts an arbitrary `tabs: &[ViewTab]` slice and validates nothing against `VIEW_TABS`, so the "exactly four" the B-runs assert is a constant, not an enforced precondition.

UNDERSPECIFIED SUB-DECISION: "saved Sheets Filter Views" names neither a source of truth nor an identity key, and the three A-runs resolved it three incompatible ways — with opposite destructive outcomes for a user-created view. A1 treats a caller/config-supplied set as authoritative and DELETES every live filter view absent from it ("the publisher owns the tab", assumption 2). A2 PRESERVES live views with no desired counterpart ("'re-assert' is additive, not exclusive", assumption 3). A3 keeps only config-owned views but prefers update-in-place over delete/recreate specifically to keep `fvid` URLs users have bookmarked stable, reading "persist across the rewrite" as identity continuity rather than mere re-existence (assumption 5). All three key matching on `title` because Sheets filter-view IDs are unstable across delete/add — itself an invention. A2 also flagged a second open reading of "regenerated" (delete-and-recreate the sheet vs clear-and-rewrite in place) and rejected the former only because it would destroy filter-view IDs. Nothing in the EARS text disambiguates any of this, so whichever behavior ships is unfalsifiable against the spec.

notes:
CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE (BD-DRIFT). Both directions converge on the same question — "what survives a republish?" — and give incompatible answers. The spec's answer: saved Filter Views survive (actively re-asserted), the tab is read-only, and basic filters / manual sorts / inserted rows do not survive. The code's answer: row 1 (the frozen typed header) survives and is contractually immutable, an AA1 STALE banner survives, saved Filter Views and basic filters survive only incidentally because the write never touches grid metadata, nothing is read-only, and inserted rows survive too on the real API because the promised tail-truncate is implemented only in the fakes. Neither side's survival contract is a subset of the other's. Finding 1 is the hinge: the A-runs implement explicit grid shrink, the B-runs assert an exact-row-count truncation guarantee — and production has neither.

METHOD NOTE: I read two files beyond the four supplied, because the supplied set could not settle whether the truncation guarantee is real — crates/runtime/src/sheets.rs (the live `SheetsApi` impl, line 510: `values.update` PUT with `valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED`, plus the unused `clear_range` at 148-150) and crates/runtime/src/testkit.rs (`FakeSheetsApi::update_range`, lines 191-205, whose `grid.truncate(start)` is the sole source of the truncation semantics). I also skimmed crates/sheets-view/tests/republish.rs (254 lines, 7 tests — serialized settle-after-write, atomic-batchupdate-with-tail-truncate, stale/banner, lock refusal), which was not in the supplied list but carries most of the behavior the B-runs reconstructed; tests/tabs.rs alone does not cover it.

A-SIDE ASSUMPTION ARTIFACTS (deliberately NOT reported as findings, per the spec-traced-vs-invented rule): single-`batchUpdate` atomicity; empty-grid legality; ragged-row non-validation; A1's reserved `ViewError::Conflict`; "no accounting/tax math here" (correct, and matches the crate boundary at lib.rs:9-10). One A-side assumption is actually HONORED and worth recording as coherent rather than drift: all three A-runs insisted values be written USER_ENTERED so the GOOGLEFINANCE column stays a live formula — the real `update_range` does exactly that (sheets.rs:511), and the trait doc at lib.rs:439-448 pins the `Cell::Value` vs `Cell::Formula` typing contract, including that `"20.0000%"` must coerce to numeric 0.20 because `=G*H` / `=G*(1-H)` multiply it.

B-SIDE OVERREACH (not reported as drift): B2's VIEW-PUB-8 and parts of B1 pull in settle-pass ordering and transient-mark carry-forward. That behavior is real (`republish_then_settle`, lib.rs:1012-1025; `read_marks` prior-carry at 873-879) but belongs to the SHEET-MARK-* specs, not to SHEET-TAB-003 — it is scope bleed from reading the whole crate, not evidence about this requirement.

STABILITY. A: high — all three runs independently produced the same three spec-traced mechanisms (ProtectedRange with warning_only=false, ClearBasicFilter, filter-view re-assert keyed by title) and the same clear-then-rewrite-whole-grid shape; their divergence is confined to the genuinely underspecified sub-decision in finding 10, which is itself the signal rather than noise. B: high — all three named `DATA_START_ROW = 2`, the `'<tab>'!A2:Z` range, the write-once/never-rewritten header with an unconditional all-builds assertion, the verbatim banner string and its `AA1` anchor, the 10-tab `workbook_tab_order()` sequence, the lock-refusal outcome, and the distinct `set_tab_order`-failure semantics (published:false with no tab flagged stale). The three B reconstructions are near-interchangeable.
